evaluations.rationale: Creating a new game is a top-level capability and does not inherently require any other backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators by giving them a URL requires that a game exists to invite them to; depends on creating a game (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: start a round
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round presupposes an existing game to start the round in; depends on game creation (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Showing all items depends on items being added or created (e.g., via add-item or start-round stories); concretely depends on adding items (PP-006) or item creation when starting a round (PP-003).

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item to be estimated requires that items exist (added or created); depends on add-item (PP-006) or start-round which creates an item (PP-003).

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding items must target a specific game/session, so it inherently requires a game to exist; depends on creating a game (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item requires items to exist (added earlier) and a game context; depends on add-item (PP-006) and game creation (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item requires items to exist and a game context; depends on add-item (PP-006) and game creation (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Revealing estimates presumes that estimators can join and submit estimates; thus depends on the ability for estimators to join (PP-029) and the estimation mechanism. Citing concrete join story (PP-029).

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average requires collected estimates, which presupposes estimators can join and submit estimates; depends on join/estimation (PP-029).

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling an estimate requires that multiple estimators can submit cards; depends on estimator participation/joining (PP-029) and the estimation mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate applies to a selected item in a game/session; depends on item selection (PP-005) and the existence of a game (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating a previous story requires prior-estimate and item selection functionality; depends on being able to select/reopen prior items (PP-005).

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories targets a specific game/session and requires that a game exists to import into; depends on creating a game (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste of stories must target a game/session; therefore depends on game creation (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games assumes games are stored from prior creation; depends on game creation and persistence (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a game's transcript presupposes the game has been created and its data stored; depends on game creation/persistence (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript requires transcript generation/viewing capability; depends on view-transcript (PP-017).

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a game's transcript requires the transcript to be available; depends on view-transcript (PP-017).

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game requires that games exist (created/stored); depends on game creation/persistence (PP-001).
Creating an account is a standalone capability and does not inherently depend on any other backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: create an account
evaluations.rationale: Logging in with an account name and password requires that accounts exist; depends on account creation (PP-021).

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details requires an existing account; depends on account creation (PP-021).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account presupposes that an account exists; depends on account creation (PP-021).
Displaying dates/times in local timezone is a presentation feature and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder presupposes accounts and stored email addresses; depends on account creation (PP-021).
Selecting a deck type for estimation is a settings feature and is not inherently dependent on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Limiting invites is directly tied to the invite-by-URL functionality; depends on invitation feature (PP-002).

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via a URL requires that the invite/URL mechanism exists to provide that page; depends on invite-by-URL (PP-002).

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the current item requires that an item has been selected or the round started; depends on selecting an item to estimate (PP-005) or start-round (PP-003).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Participant view of the full item list depends on the moderator/host-side capability to show or provide the list (PP-004).

evaluations.evidence: see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Indicating who has given an estimate presupposes participants can join and submit estimates; depends on join/estimation functionality (PP-029).

evaluations.evidence: shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates after all have given requires the join/estimation mechanism to collect those estimates; depends on estimator participation/joining (PP-029).

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Changing estimates until the draw completes depends on the definition and implementation of draw completion and simultaneous reveal (PP-033).

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior estimates for the same story requires storage or navigation to prior rounds/estimates (e.g., scroll-back functionality PP-039); depends on that storage/navigation capability.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Showing identity alongside estimates relies on the simultaneous-reveal/display mechanism (PP-033) and identity tracking; depends on reveal/display story (PP-033).
Providing a shared countdown timer is a standalone UI/interaction feature and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Automatic timer reset on 'we all play an estimate' requires the timer feature (PP-037) and the mechanism that detects when all estimates are played (PP-033).

Scrolling back through prior rounds is a session UI capability and does not inherently require a different backlog story to exist first (it may build on stored data but no single concrete backlog story is specified as prerequisite).
Keeping card order consistent across draws is a stand-alone presentation requirement and does not inherently depend on other specific backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: The ability to change an estimate up to draw completion presupposes a defined draw-completion/reveal mechanism (PP-033); thus it depends on that story.
Displaying a thumbnail near where cards are played is a UI enhancement and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.
Compliance with XHTML/CSS standards is a quality goal that is independent of other functional backlog stories.
Maintaining a list of definitions is an independent documentation task and does not inherently require other stories.
Creating database indexes is a technical task and not an inherent dependency on other backlog stories per the non-technical-dependency rule.
Ensuring functionality in specified browsers is an implementation/compatibility goal and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.
Accessibility compliance is a cross-cutting concern and is not inherently dependent on other specific backlog stories.
Improving responsiveness is a general performance requirement and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.
Unicode support is a platform requirement that does not inherently require another backlog story.
Sensible/predictable URLs is a design requirement independent of other backlog stories.
Having nice error pages is a presentation/UX requirement and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.
Storing research results non-identifiably is a data-handling requirement and does not inherently require another specific backlog story to exist first.
Providing usage metrics is a feature request that can be implemented independently (though it requires data collection), but no single backlog story is a prerequisite.
